config.question: Does a second model family, TabPFN over frozen pretrained molecular features, pick better batches or predict more accurately than Aster's Morgan-fingerprint ridge default on the same time-ordered splits?
config.hypothesis: Stated before the run: on a few hundred to a few thousand measurements per endpoint, TabPFN's in-context fit is expected to beat ridge on accuracy by a small margin and to be indistinguishable on the batch-selection metric, because selection depends on the ranking of the top of the pool rather than on average error. A null result is reported as a null.
config.base_config_note: Splits, endpoints, transforms, minimum sizes and the batch criteria are inherited from the temporal protocol rather than restated, so that bracket numbers can be read beside docs/TEMPORAL_RESULTS.md.
config.bracket_note: A bracket logs both families per case. The product default is not replaced by a result in this file; queue item 11 asks for a deliberate two-model bracket, and replacing the default would need its own decision.
config.control_seeds_note: Five matched random splits per endpoint, against the twenty the temporal error study uses, because each case here fits a transformer per arm rather than a ridge. The power accounting in the output reports what the pairs can detect at this count.

chemeleon.description: Frozen CheMeleon embeddings, the pretrained molecular representation already pinned in configs/transfer-v1.json. No assay label enters feature generation.

tabpfn.description: TabPFN: a transformer pretrained on synthetic tables that predicts a new table in one forward pass, with no gradient training on the assay data.
tabpfn.checkpoint_note: Not downloaded by this code. Prior Labs distribute the weights through Hugging Face under their own licence, and recent package releases require a one-time licence acceptance and an API token. Put the checkpoint at this path, then replace the placeholder with its sha256sum; a run with the placeholder in place stops rather than using unpinned weights.
tabpfn.feature_budget_note: Columns kept for a TabPFN arm, chosen by variance across the training rows only. TabPFN is built for tables of at most a few hundred columns; a 2048-bit fingerprint and a 2048-wide embedding are both outside that regime.

reporting.pairing: Each arm is compared with the default on the identical endpoint, split and seed, so the unit of analysis is a paired per-case difference.
reporting.null_handling: A mean difference near zero is reported with the minimum detectable effect beside it and is never described as equivalence.

normalised_mae.spread_source: case-to-case spread of morgan_ridge's own normalised_mae
normalised_mae.interpretation: The smallest difference a bracket of this many cases could detect at 80% power, assuming paired differences are as spread out as the metric itself. Pairing normally does better than that, so treat it as an upper bound.
